title: 영어브리핑_2026-10-30
korean_summary: 내일 핵심: Kasun 방문 시각·봉제 대응자 아침에 확정, 08:00 Foodinco 지붕 수리 확인·사진, 원사 미신고 표 받아 오전 법인장 보고(토 실사 전)
paragraphs: Good morning, Anthony. Today is Friday, October thirtieth. It is the last workday before the physical count on Saturday.
Rain is expected from today until November fourth. So today is a busy day, inside and outside the factory.

We have eight parts today. Part one is the top three for today. Part two is the reports to collect. Part three is the replies you owe. Part four is the schedule and deadlines. Part five is English review. Part six is a role-play. Part seven is the closing. And part eight is a short recap of your first three actions.
Let's start.
Part one. Top three for today.
Number one. Mr Kasun from Aritzia visits the factory today.

What is it? He will check the trim liability and the disposal of B grade goods. B grade means second quality garments. As of yesterday, we still had no visit time in the mail. We also had no person named to meet him from the sewing side.

Why does it matter? Chamin leaves the company tomorrow, on October thirty-first. Channa is not here. So nobody may be ready to answer his sewing questions. A buyer visit with no clear host looks bad. It can also cause mistakes on the liability numbers.

Your first action. Call or message Lency at the start of the day. Ask for the visit time and the plan. Then name one person from sewing to join. Make sure the trim liability list and the B grade list are printed before he comes.
Number two. Foodinco will fix the roof leaks today at eight in the morning.
What is it? Ms Trinh Tran, the chief accountant, said Foodinco's contractor comes at eight. Foodinco is our landlord. They will fix the leaks in the factory roof.

Why does it matter? Rain starts today and lasts about six days. If the repair is not done, water can reach the cutting area and the fabric. Yesterday you asked Ms Trinh Tran for two things. First, which areas they will fix. Second, before and after photos.

Your first action. At eight, check that the contractor has arrived. Ask Ms Trinh Tran for the list of repair areas. If the rain stops the work, ask for the new date right away. Also check the forty sandbags at the emergency exits in the cutting section.
Number three. The thread with no customs declaration.
What is it? Some Aritzia thread from COATS PHONG PHU came in without an import declaration. The invoice was in the name of POONGIN TRADING, not our factory. This is now six days old.

Why does it matter? The physical count is tomorrow. If we count thread that is not declared, the customs balance will not match. Mr Moon has not received a report yet. We need a direction before the count.

Your first action. Get the table from Trinh Do in exports and imports. The table shows invoice number, date received, quantity, and current stock. Then write a short report to Mr Moon this morning. Give him the facts and two or three options.
Those are the top three. Kasun visit, roof repair, and the undeclared thread.
Part two. Reports to collect.
These are reports other people owe you today.

First, Trinh Do in exports and imports. She owes two things. One is the thread table for the customs issue. The other is the check list before the count. Yesterday she said some numbers did not match the warehouse sheet. You told her the list is old, from October twenty-third. She only needs to fill the blank lines in "Result and Remark."
Here is a sentence you can use. "Trinh, please send me the thread table by ten, and fill in only the blank lines in the check list."
Second, Mint in the fabric warehouse. Before the count, Rack seven and Rack eight must be ready. Fabric with no rack must be marked. Interlining must be kept separate.
Here is a sentence. "Mint, could you confirm whether Rack seven and Rack eight are ready for tomorrow's count?"

Third, Ms Tho in human resources. You asked for the number of leave forms from Line one in October. You asked for the number by leave type. The deadline is today. You also asked about one worker. She shows annual leave on October ninth and twelfth, but she is not on Ms Tho's list.
Here is a sentence. "Ms Tho, just a reminder that the Line one leave form numbers are due today."

Fourth, Mai in purchasing. You chose the Malaysia Airlines flight for Mr Asanka on November tenth. Mai must book it and raise the purchase request. A purchase request is called a PR. Mai also still owes the consumables ledger update and the new quotes for the relaxing racks. Those were due on Wednesday and Thursday.
Here is a sentence. "Mai, please update me as soon as the flight is booked, and send me the e-ticket."
Fifth, Ms Trinh Tran for the IRC. IRC means investment registration certificate. Ms Van is drafting a decision for the IRC change. It was expected yesterday afternoon. Mr Moon must sign it.
Here is a sentence. "Ms Trinh, when will you be able to send me the draft decision for Mr Moon?"
Sixth, Ms Ly in human resources. She must update October working hours. You asked her to finish by Saturday. Head office needs it by eleven on Monday.
Here is a sentence. "Ms Ly, please keep me posted on the working hours update until it is done."
Part three. Replies you owe.

First, Mr Asanka, the new sewing manager. He wrote yesterday afternoon. He said the baggage allowance is enough. But he needs a visa or an appointment letter to show his bank. Your reply should help him with that. Check with Ms Tho first about the e-visa status.
A good first sentence is this. "Dear Mr Asanka, thank you for your reply. We will send you the appointment letter today, and the e-visa as soon as it is issued."

Second, Mr Moon about two things. One is the thread with no customs declaration. The other is good news. Mr Asanka will arrive on November tenth, and the flight is chosen. You can report both in one short message.
A good first sentence is this. "Mr Moon, I'd like to update you on two points: the undeclared thread and Mr Asanka's arrival."

Third, Ms Trinh Tran about the environmental permit. The industrial park board now wants a notarized copy of the factory lease. A notarized copy needs Mr Moon's real signature. A signature stamp cannot be used. So you need to arrange a time with Mr Moon to sign.
A good first sentence is this. "Ms Trinh, thank you for explaining. I will ask Mr Moon to sign the lease agreement and the decision together."

Fourth, Mr Quan in IT. He replied about the SSD plan. SSD means the computer storage drive. He said D zero five one is not really spare. A new intern uses it, but the intern is not on the HR list. You need to clarify this.
A good first sentence is this. "Mr Quan, thank you. Could you tell me the intern's name and start date, so I can check with HR?"
Fifth, approvals. Two debit payments arrived yesterday in the groupware. One is for Aritzia woven, from Lency. The other is for J Crew, from Ms Thao. Please approve them if they are correct.
Part four. Schedule and deadlines.

Today, Friday, October thirtieth. Eight in the morning, Foodinco roof repair. Some time today, Mr Kasun's visit. Also today, the security pledge completion report for local staff. Also the third quarter corporate income tax prepayment. Also the count list mail to the chief accountant. And the Line one leave numbers from Ms Tho. Friday also means the weekly cash flow report and the weekly outsourcing report.

Tomorrow, Saturday, October thirty-first. The fabric and thread physical count. Chamin's last day. The September export and import ledger from Trinh Do. The logistics cost report for January to June. Ms Ly's working hours. And the short-term payroll review for the November third payment.
Sunday is off.

Monday, November second. Head office working hours deadline at eleven. Electricity and water bills arrive and must be uploaded. The weekly wood fuel report. And the monthly Korean staff annual leave data to head office.
Tuesday, November third. The J Crew pre-production meeting moved to that day.
Part five. English review.
We will practice ten expressions. Some are from yesterday, some from two and four days ago, and some from last week.

The expression is "discrepancy." It means a difference between two numbers or two records that should match. For example, "Could you explain the discrepancy between the check list and the warehouse sheet?" Now say it with me.
One more time. Could you explain the discrepancy between the check list and the warehouse sheet?
The expression is "prioritize." It means to do something first because it is more important. For example, "Please prioritize the thread table before the count list." Now say it with me.
One more time. Please prioritize the thread table before the count list.
The expression is "advise." In business English, it means to tell or inform. For example, "Please advise us of the visit time for Mr Kasun." Now say it with me.
One more time. Please advise us of the visit time for Mr Kasun.
The expression is "If something is not done by a time, we will have to do something." For example, "If the roof is not fixed by noon, we will have to move the fabric." Now say it with me.
One more time. If the roof is not fixed by noon, we will have to move the fabric.
The expression is "clarify." It means to make something clear. For example, "Please clarify who uses D zero five one." Now say it with me.
One more time. Please clarify who uses D zero five one.
The expression is "mandatory." It means you must do it. It is not optional. For example, "A real signature is mandatory for the notarized lease." Now say it with me.
One more time. A real signature is mandatory for the notarized lease.

The expression is "Is there any way that something can happen?" It is a polite way to ask for a solution. For example, "Is there any way the contractor can finish before the rain?" Now say it with me.
One more time. Is there any way the contractor can finish before the rain?
The expression is "justify." It means to give a good reason for something. For example, "Please justify the price of the new rack quotes." Now say it with me.
One more time. Please justify the price of the new rack quotes.

The expression is "outstanding." Here it does not mean excellent. It means not done or not received yet. For example, "The consumables ledger and the rack quotes are still outstanding." Now say it with me.
One more time. The consumables ledger and the rack quotes are still outstanding.
The last expression is "feasible." It means possible to do in real life. For example, "Is it feasible to finish the count before noon?" Now say it with me.
One more time. Is it feasible to finish the count before noon?
Good. "Outstanding" and "feasible" were wrong in last week's test. So please use them in a mail today.
Part six. Role-play.
The situation is your short report to Mr Moon this morning. The topic is the thread with no customs declaration. Listen first.
Anthony says, "Good morning, Mr Moon. I'd like to update you on the thread without customs declaration."
Mr Moon says, "Yes. What is the problem?"
Anthony says, "Some Aritzia thread came in under POONGIN TRADING's invoice. So our factory did not declare it."
Mr Moon says, "How much thread is it?"
Anthony says, "Trinh Do sent a table this morning. It shows the quantity, the date received, and the current stock."
Mr Moon says, "The count is tomorrow. What should we do?"
Anthony says, "There are two options. First, we declare it now, before the count. Second, we keep it separate and count it as not ours."
Mr Moon says, "Which one do you recommend?"
Anthony says, "I recommend the first option. It keeps our customs balance correct. But we need head office to send the invoice in our name."
Mr Moon says, "Okay. Please ask head office today."
Anthony says, "I will. I will also tell Mint to keep the thread separate until it is declared."
Mr Moon says, "Good. Keep me posted."
Anthony says, "Yes. I will update you before the count."
Now let's practice two key sentences.
The first sentence. "I'd like to update you on the thread without customs declaration." Say it with me.
One more time. I'd like to update you on the thread without customs declaration.
The second sentence. "I recommend the first option. It keeps our customs balance correct." Say it with me.
One more time. I recommend the first option. It keeps our customs balance correct.
Great job.
Part seven. Closing.
Today has one main goal. Finish everything the count and the buyer visit need, before the rain and before Saturday.

Remember, many people owe you something today. Do not wait for them. Ask early in the morning, and ask once more after lunch. Use short and clear sentences. Give a time for every request. And when a reply comes, check the file yourself before you close the item.
Part eight. Your first three actions.
First, confirm Mr Kasun's visit time with Lency, and name one sewing person to join.
Second, at eight, check the Foodinco roof repair and ask Ms Trinh Tran for photos.
Third, get the thread table from Trinh Do and report to Mr Moon this morning.
That's all for today. Have a good Friday, Anthony. See you tomorrow, on Saturday, for the count.
